metadata.title: organize: read DICOM inside zip archives
metadata.notes: Release v0.1.1 and the 20-folder OSC subset rerun are manual, after merge (spec: Release check).

tasks.title: Zip staging: classify, cap, allow-list and extract one folder's zips (pure function, no wiring)
tasks.test_approach: TDD in a new tests/test_organize_zip.py. Zips are built at test time with zipfile from synthetic DICOM (tests/synthetic_dicom.py) and raw bytes; corrupt variants are made by byte edits (CRC flip, truncation, compress_type patched to 9 in both headers, encrypted flag bit set, invalid-UTF-8 name with the UTF-8 flag). Caps are monkeypatched low. No real data.
criteria: AC1: _has_preamble itself does the one 132-byte read and returns 'dicom' (DICM at offset 128), 'zip' (first 4 bytes PK\x03\x04) or None (anything else, an empty zip PK\x05\x06 included); the zip pre-pass and _read_one both branch on its result, so tests that monkeypatch org._has_preamble keep working. A staged file that classifies as 'zip' is not DICOM and is never opened. _read_one returns None unless the result is 'dicom' (a loose or staged zip is never passed to read_header_core).

AC2: A folder's zips (sorted walk order, numbered from 1) are extracted into a given staging sub-folder as <zip #>/<member #> (infolist order, from 1), each member streamed through ZipFile.open(); directory members are skipped; a member that is itself a zip is staged as a plain file and never opened; a symlink entry is staged as a regular file of its bytes.
AC3: Members named ../x.dcm, /abs/x.dcm and two members with one name all land inside the staging sub-folder, and both same-name members are staged.

AC4: Caps are checked from the central directory over all zips of the folder before any member is written: declared file_size sum > MAX_UNZIP_BYTES (16 GiB) or non-directory member count > MAX_ZIP_MEMBERS (200,000) is a cap failure; nothing is staged.
AC5: A member with flag_bits & 0x61 != 0 or compress_type outside {0, 8, 12, 14} makes its zip unreadable before extraction.

AC6: BadZipFile, EOFError, zlib.error, lzma.LZMAError, UnicodeDecodeError, NotImplementedError and RuntimeError while opening or reading a zip mark it unreadable (CRC flip, truncated archive, method 9, encrypted, invalid-UTF-8 name each tested); OSError propagates unchanged.

AC7: A bad zip in a folder with at least one loose file carrying the DICM preamble is skipped (its staged members removed, counted as skipped); in a folder with no such loose file it is a refusal with the fixed REASON_ZIP_TOO_LARGE (a cap) or REASON_ZIP_UNREADABLE (anything else), and nothing staged remains; an over-cap total in a folder with loose DICOM skips every zip of the folder.

AC8: The extraction function returns the staged paths plus counts (zips, zip members, zips skipped), or raises a private ZipRefused(reason) with `from None` carrying REASON_ZIP_TOO_LARGE or REASON_ZIP_UNREADABLE; caplog for the traversal, CRC and encrypted cases (member names starting SYNTHETIC_PATIENT_NAME) holds no member name or path. Reason texts (exact): REASON_ZIP_TOO_LARGE = 'zip archives in the source folder exceed the size or member cap; nothing kept'; REASON_ZIP_UNREADABLE = 'a zip archive in the source folder cannot be read safely; nothing kept'; REASON_LOCKED = 'another organize run holds the output root lock'.
Guardrail: refusal reasons are fixed module-level string constants (profile review rule); no zipfile exception text reaches any log line or message.

tasks.title: Wire zips into organize: staging parent, task A/B contract, link-or-copy, lifetime, lock, summary line
tasks.test_approach: TDD through organize() on synthetic exports written to tmp_path, zipped at test time. Lifecycle tests patch zipfile or dicom_io.read_header_core (not _read_fn) so real extraction runs; KeyboardInterrupt is raised from a patched member read. workers=2 runs the real process pool. Existing _read_fn/_copy_fn fakes in tests/test_organize.py are updated to the new tuple only. The KeyboardInterrupt-during-extraction test runs with workers=1 (in-process; pool workers are spawned, so monkeypatches do not reach them). The workers=2 cleanup test uses no patches, or a module-level helper in tests/pool_workers.py.
criteria: AC9: organize() creates one staging parent out_root/.unzip-<random>/ (tempfile.mkdtemp) in the parent process and passes it to task A in the task args; task A extracts the folder's zips into a fresh sub-folder before any header read, and staged files go through the existing read and grouping unchanged; staged members count in files walked. Staged paths are appended after the sorted loose paths. The staging parent is a new task A argument after skip_root; the result tuple becomes (name, refusal, cases, misc, unreadable, walked, reading, staging, zips, zip_members, zips_skipped).

AC10: Task A's result gains staging (Path | None), zips, zip_members, zips_skipped; _copy_patient gains the staging path; task B hard-links each staged file into every destination folder (os.link, falling back to a copy, as masks._link_or_copy), copies loose files as today, and removes the staging sub-folder in a finally.

AC11: A synthetic patient (CT + RTSTRUCT + RTPLAN chain plus one MR series) exported as one zip organizes and then converts to the same plan and study outputs (same series, same voxels) as the same files loose.

AC12: Loose files plus a zip holding the rest organize as one patient; one instance present both loose and zipped is deduplicated by SOP: the loose copy is used (staged paths come after loose ones) and the zipped copy goes to misc_files.
AC13: A zipped patient with two RTPLANs on one planning CT: both plan folders hold the full CT series.

AC14: _read_patient catches ZipRefused and returns the refusal tuple (sanitized folder name, reads_kept=False) like its len(ids) != 1 branch, so _worker never sees it and the run is not aborted. Zip-only folders over a cap give a REASON_ZIP_TOO_LARGE row and with an unreadable zip a REASON_ZIP_UNREADABLE row, with the sanitized folder name and reads_kept=False (with --overwrite an existing output folder is untouched); the next patient of the same run still organizes. Loose DICOM plus a bad zip organizes from the loose files and the log says 1 zips skipped.

AC15: No .unzip-* remains under out_root after: success, refusal, skip of an existing output (reachable only after full extraction, as the name comes from the headers; task A's cases=None return removes its own staging), an OSError from the classification read (patch org._has_preamble as test_organize.py does; task A's own except BaseException removes staging, since _worker's failure row names none), a REASON_INTERNAL abort, KeyboardInterrupt during extraction, and a workers=2 run; if the staging parent cannot be removed, one fixed warning with a count is logged.

AC15b: Per-branch cleanup: task A wraps its work in try/except BaseException: remove sub-folder; raise, and removes its sub-folder itself on a refusal and on the cases=None skip; handle() removes the sub-folder a task-A result names in every branch that does not submit task B (aborted, name claimed, recover OSError, existing-target skip). Tests assert the staging parent is empty right after _read_patient returns for the refusal, skip and OSError cases, and after a name-claimed refusal in a two-folder run, not only at run end.

AC16: Lock order in organize(): (1) the two existing ValueError checks, then mkdir of out_root; (2) open out_root/.organize.lock and fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) (fcntl imported inside a platform guard, not at module top level; on Windows no lock); only BlockingIOError becomes ValueError(REASON_LOCKED), any other OSError from opening or flocking the lock file (e.g. a cluster file system without flock) logs one fixed warning and the run continues with no lock and no leftover sweep, as on Windows (sweeping unlocked could delete a live run's staging); (3) remove leftover .unzip-* folders, then mkdtemp the staging parent; (4) enter the existing try, whose finally removes the staging parent and releases the lock. A refused second run writes no report (the live run's organize_report.csv is untouched). The lock file stays on disk. REASON_LOCKED is added to the __main__.py fixed refusal list; a CLI test shows a second run on a held lock exits 1 with 'rt_dataprep: <REASON_LOCKED>' and empty stdout. Reason texts (exact): REASON_ZIP_TOO_LARGE = 'zip archives in the source folder exceed the size or member cap; nothing kept'; REASON_ZIP_UNREADABLE = 'a zip archive in the source folder cannot be read safely; nothing kept'; REASON_LOCKED = 'another organize run holds the output root lock'.

AC17: The organize summary line format becomes '..., %d unreadable files, %d zips, %d zip members, %d zips skipped; %d replaced, %d kept' (zip counts before the semicolon); organize_report.csv columns are unchanged; convert run on an output root holding .organize.lock reads no patient from it.

AC18: The full existing suite passes; the only existing-test changes are the fake return tuples (and new task A argument) in tests/pool_workers.py, the updated summary-line pattern if needed, and the tests/test_organize.py helpers listing()/hidden()/snapshot() ignoring the persistent .organize.lock (no assertion is otherwise edited).

Guardrail: pydicom reads of staged files stay inside dicom_io._pydicom_quiet() for the whole folder read (vault: pydicom-validates-lazily-on-first-tag-access); source trees are only read (zips opened read-only, never moved or deleted).

tasks.title: Docs: zip support in README
tasks.test_approach: Docs only; the full suite and ruff stay green.
criteria: AC19: README's organize section states that zip archives in a source folder are read (stored, deflate, bzip2, lzma; no encryption, no nesting, no tar/7z), the 16 GiB / 200,000-member per-folder caps, the bad-zip skip-or-refuse rule with both reason texts, the hidden .unzip-* staging and the POSIX-only .organize.lock, and the new summary-line counts. It also says a killed run's leftover .unzip-* is removed by the next run, and that staged files appear in plan folders under index names (1, 1_1, ...).
